candidates.prompt_content: When an execution unit authors or modifies a precommitted schedule, history commitment, salt, or any ordering that later selects targets or truncates search, derive that value only from stable behavior semantics: program descriptors, support examples, domains, and digest-ranked schedule content. Never fold whole run reports, engine run ids, trial-ledger bytes, timestamps, or other per-process values into such a commitment; a reproducibility check (two fresh processes, identical seed and tree, identical selection) is part of the unit's evidence. The compliant in-repo pattern is evidence_derived_target_synthesis.py; the violation pattern to avoid is folding a full evidence report digest into a selection salt.
candidates.risk: An over-broad reading could forbid legitimate audit digests or force sorting costs onto hot paths; the rule binds only values consumed by selection, ordering, or truncation, and the reproducibility check bounds trial cost to one duplicate process run per authored commitment.

result.rationale: Expected-time ranking under agi/WORK_STRATEGY.json: every future campaign stacked on the recursive frontier currently inherits a per-run selection lottery, which already forced PR 245's end-to-end diagnostic to exclude the recursive member from assertions entirely and blocks reproducible end-to-end evidence for any successor capability (including a future return of the observed-schema family). Repairing the single verified leak point restores determinism for the whole chain at the cost of one bounded code unit with a mechanical proof, which dominates starting any new capability family on top of a non-reproducible prerequisite. The saturation assessment continues to bar new same-family retention probes, and the CLI binding hardening remains queued as the subsequent smaller unit.
